allie-2.0.description: Allie predicts human move choices from the sequence of moves played in a game. Use a position with recorded moves. The local model requires substantial storage and memory.
allie-2.0.rating: Depends on the model and rating input

allie-2.1.description: Allie predicts human move choices from the sequence of moves played in a game. Use a position with recorded moves. The local model requires substantial storage and memory.
allie-2.1.rating: Depends on the model and rating input

custom.description: Runs an executable you supply that supports UCI, the standard chess engine protocol. Available features depend on that executable.
custom.rating: See the engine’s own rating or settings

flounder.description: Uses Stockfish to compare moves, then samples from its candidates to vary the quality of play. The target is approximate and its choices come from a mistake model.

gaia.description: A UCI chess engine written in Rust with a neural evaluation network. It searches for strong moves and can use an approximate optional strength limit.

lc0.description: Leela Chess Zero uses a network trained by playing itself. It explores positions to choose strong moves. A CPU run or smaller network can change its speed and strength.
lc0.rating: Strength varies with the network, hardware and search time

maia1-1100.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1100 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1200.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1200 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1300.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1300 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1400.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1400 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1500.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1500 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1600.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1600 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1700.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1700 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1800.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1800 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia1-1900.description: Uses a network trained on human games near 1900 Elo. The weights fix the rating band. The LC0 runtime runs the model with a one-node search.

maia2.description: Predicts moves from real rapid games. BoardLens maps the input rating to Maia-2’s training bands. The selected rating describes whose moves it tries to predict.

maia3-23m.description: Mid-sized model with higher resource needs. It predicts moves human players at the chosen rating are likely to make. The target describes the players it models.

maia3-5m.description: Smallest model for faster CPU predictions. It predicts moves human players at the chosen rating are likely to make. The target describes the players it models.

maia3-79m.description: Largest model with the highest memory and compute needs. It predicts moves human players at the chosen rating are likely to make. The target describes the players it models.

neural-chess.description: This compact network learns from human move choices across games. It ranks likely legal moves using the current position, with a single prediction pass in BoardLens.

rodent.description: A search engine with configurable personalities. Its settings can change which positions and plans it favors. Select a supported local Rodent executable to use it.
rodent.rating: Depends on the imported build and personality

stockfish.description: Calculates lines and scores positions. Full strength and skill 20 let it search at its strongest settings. Lower skill or a rating limit deliberately weakens its move choices. On Android, select strength with the skill control.
stockfish.rating: Desktop rating limit: 1320–3190 Elo on supported builds. Benchmark example: Stockfish 18 64-bit 4CPU scored 3649 in CCRL 40/15.

tiny153.description: Looks one move ahead and favors safe squares and simple development. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny17.description: Tries to mirror the opponent’s moves when it can. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny253.description: Favors active pieces, advancing pawns and king safety. Deep tactics can trip it up. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny266.description: Searches for positions where pieces reach useful squares. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny278.description: Plays the Bongcloud, then favors obvious captures, promotions and mate before picking other moves. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny303.description: Searches ahead and values how freely and safely its pieces can move. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny425.description: Uses a compact search focused on material and how freely pieces can move. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny529.description: Uses a compact neural network to score positions in its search. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny610.description: Searches deeply and scores how well pieces are placed. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny614.description: Searches deeply for tactics and considers mobility, piece placement and pawn structure. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny628.description: Searches deeply and can steer its own king into an attack. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

tiny70.description: Searches ahead and emphasizes material and gaining time against opposing pieces. The rating comes from the Tiny Chess Bots competition. BoardLens uses one suggested move per search.

toby.description: Toby predicts human moves and uses an engine to assess them. On Mac, the Engine Library installs Fast mode with Maia-3 79M and Stockfish. Set the target rating, search time and number of recommendations.
